result.summary: The spec is written and measured at 18cb9e04: 114,387 bytes, pure ASCII, LF, and git status --short is still empty. It covers migration 048, which adds compare_runs (the closed column list of R-S22-2) and compare_judgements, compare_runs_prune, and the delete_user_cascade redefinition: the 043 body plus one kb_feedback DELETE inserted at chunk index 2, before the first detach UPDATE. It also covers the leaf app/services/compare_runs.py (the flag is read first; a pure 21-key row builder; one fire-and-forget run_db insert through the admin client, with one WARNING line on failure). Each of the five delivery exits gets one plain call: text_routes :885 / :1090 / :1482, image_routes :782 and url_routes :392. Last is scripts/cron_compare_judge.py with railway.judge.json: the re-compare flag, the programmatic checks, one Haiku batch per run in the G2 pattern on the offclock lane, a capped Sonnet escalation on the escalation lane, writes and prunes in apply mode only, and a counts-only report. Measurements that matter: (1) the comparison_id is on the body before the exit only on the three text exits, and only with ENABLE_COMPARISON_ID_ECHO ON and a signed-in user, which sets the L-LINK limit. (2) The R-S22-10 statement as written, with its 'AS f' alias, cannot be parsed by the 043 fence's _DEL_RX, which would turn four pins red; the spec drops the alias (Q1). (3) The 045 header gives kb_prune_feedback(365) to S81-22's nightly job, and nothing calls it today (Q3). (4) The body carries no KB product id, so kb_product_ids is NULL (Q4). (5) data_coverage is an integer from 0 to 4, typed smallint. (6) docs/privacy-data-inventory.md is the iOS manifest inventory read by client fences, so it is not edited (Q11). The base pass state was run twice through pyt.py, both OK: 817 passed and 1058 passed.

blocking: B1 (measured pin collision): add an E-row to tests/test_migration_043_delete_user_cascade.py that limits the two mutant rows (dropped DELETE :1192, weakened predicate :1204) to fence user tables. Add it to section 3, section 4.1 and gate 4, and remove the file from the 4.2 'unedited' list.

B2 (spend: double billing): a batch that does not end within JUDGE_MAX_WAIT_SECONDS is left pending with no --resume and no stored batch id. The next night submits the same runs in a new batch, while the first batch is still billed, never read or ledgered, and never deleted (its data persists 29 days). Rule cancel-on-timeout, a durable pending record that the next run resumes, or a G2-style --resume, and add a J row.

B3 (spend: repeat Haiku calls): runs left with judged_at NULL (escalation_capped, refused, breaker_off) are re-batched to Haiku every night inside JUDGE_WINDOW_DAYS, which can be up to 30 nights. Skip runs that already have a haiku judgement row.
contract_risks: K1 (legal truth): R-S12-18 says kb_feedback is deleted with the account's compare records. The hook only reaches runs with a comparison_id, which needs ENABLE_COMPARISON_ID_ECHO ON (it is OFF in production), so the deletion part of that sentence would be false.

K2: The judge's Sonnet calls share LANE_ESCALATION, and its daily cap (default 1.0 USD), with the live router's escalations (llm_router :1120, :1129, :1213). A nightly run can starve live escalations for the rest of that Riyadh day.

K3: The verdict prose in the evidence snapshot can carry cohort- or profile-shaped text into the Anthropic batch, which conflicts with 'strip profile/cohort before any batch' (PLAN_S81 :114, R-S22-5).
K4: OpenTelemetry names are unverified. gen_ai.operation.name is an operation-kind enum, not a role, and the cache attribute spelling may differ in current semantic conventions.
K5: The refusal_reason CHECK ^[a-z_]{1,64}$ excludes the house's upper-case refusal codes, which S81-22b will need.
K6: The hook deletes every kb_feedback row sharing a linked compare_request_id, including forged or reused ids. That is safe for privacy, but the 7.3 story must be worded precisely.
K7: Confirmed with no change: response keys, request fields, refusal shapes, credits, T23, the FY25 / w4_11 digests, the s10 goldens, the W4-13 fixture and the camera envelope.
corrections: C1: P01 contradicts itself. Replacing record_compare_run with a raising stub would make every flag-OFF request raise, because the route calls it unconditionally. Keep the real function; put raising stubs on build_run_row / _insert / _query_hmac and recorders on fire_and_forget / run_db / the admin client.
C2: R03 must say how a leading docstring is treated (skip it, or forbid one).
C3: Migration 050 (llm_spend_ledger) is written but not applied. Make it an apply precondition of ENABLE_BATCH_JUDGE, or the spend is recorded only as a WARNING line.
C4: common.log_counts calls int(v) on every value; the 2.12 report holds nested dicts, so it raises TypeError. Log a flattened counts dict.

C5: The self-produced routing checks any call in llm_calls, which is broader than R-S22-7's field-level rule. Once S81-06 is on, nearly every run is Haiku-produced, so the batch would be skipped and runs would pile up as escalation_capped.
C6: A run that leaves JUDGE_WINDOW_DAYS with judged_at NULL is never judged again. Name this state 'unjudged-expired' for D22b instead of 'pending'.
C7: JUDGE_ESCALATION_MAX_PER_RUN is per script run, while PLAN_S81 :114 / :168 ask for daily count caps. Make it per Riyadh day or state the limit.
C8: Spell out that the reserve happens only when the breaker is ON (the G2 form at :513-520). Add a breaker-OFF row asserting zero reserve / settle / record calls.

C9: The user-'wrong' trigger is inert in production (the echo is OFF, so comparison_id is NULL; no compare_request_id column exists at base). Pin the comparison_feedback select to (comparison_id, winner_correct) only.
C10: P04 / P05 / PJ1 hold 64-hex literals. Their constant names must avoid the gitleaks keywords; DEVICE_KEY_* would block the commit.
C11: The recorder that stands in for fire_and_forget should close the unscheduled coroutines (to avoid RuntimeWarning noise).

C12: Once 048 is applied, rolling back 045 alone breaks every account deletion with 42P01. State in the header and the APPLY files that 048 is rolled back before 045; any failure in the hook aborts the whole deletion.
C13: The alias-free hook text is correct for _DEL_RX, but no form of the statement leaves the 043 fence file unedited (see B1).

refuted_claims: R1: Section 4.2 says the 043 fence pins (:1055-1300) stay green and unedited with 048 present. MEASURED false. With a probe 048 (the 043 body plus the alias-free kb_feedback DELETE), tests/test_migration_043_delete_user_cascade.py::test_fence_flags_each_dropped_delete (:1192) and ::test_fence_flags_each_weakened_delete_predicate (:1204) go red with AssertionError ('kb_feedback', []). Both rows walk every DELETE statement in the latest definition, and kb_feedback is not a fence user table, so a DELETE of it produces no gap. The alias form fails test_cascade_erases_or_keeps_every_user_referencing_table instead (the 'unrecognised statement' gap at :546). Either form needs an E-row.

R2: J27 says a snapshot carrying </EVIDENCE> is neutralised. False. sanitize_untrusted_block (prompt_sanitizer :55-72) only neutralises USER_INPUT and SEARCH_RESULTS tags (regex at :13), and json.dumps does not escape < or >.
R3: R26 (no gitleaks keyword in any new module-level name) fails on the spec's own names: ROW_KEYS, LLM_CALL_KEYS (2.2) and JUDGE_MAX_TOKENS (2.10).

R4: Mutant M21 (camera line moved before the envelope arm) is EQUIVALENT. The arm fires only when not success (image_routes :629, :772), and record_compare_run returns on success is not True, so no row can kill it.

R5: Section 1.6 says the ledger is visible at the exit for every input type. Not for URL: the URL path binds no OpenAI ledger (start_openai_ledger is called only at scs :4293 / :4954 and image_routes :376; compare_from_urls never reaches scs), so URL rows get llm_calls None. Camera rows lose the vision calls: the compare's own bind replaces the ContextVar, and the route keeps vision_ledger as a local (:376, :648, :679).
R6: Section 2.9.3 says the ruling left column types to the spec. R-S22-2 states data_coverage text NULL explicitly; the spec silently retypes it to smallint instead of raising a question.

R7: Citation drift in seed_kb_batch: _anthropic_factory is at :92 (spec :91), build_requests :249 (:248), anthropic_usage_record :479 (:478), breaker :513 (:510), reserve :517 (:514). Every other cited line re-measured correctly.
